edits.old: Microsoft documents /32 private-endpoint routes that propagate across configured VNet peerings. A first-hand Azure hub-and-spoke report describes a Storage private-endpoint return path bypassing the hub firewall, and commenters discuss asymmetric inspection and SNAT. Use this as general Azure troubleshooting evidence; it does not establish Atlas-specific behavior or universal cross-spoke connectivity. (low confidence)
edits.new: Microsoft documents that the /32 private-endpoint route is propagated to any configured virtual network peering. A 2022 practitioner blog post (msandbu.org) describes a Storage account private endpoint in a hub-and-spoke setup where Azure Firewall network rules forward traffic without SNAT, so the endpoint sends the reply directly back to the VM and bypasses the firewall, and the VM drops the session. In that post's comments, a reader asks whether an NVA firewall has the same issue and the author answers that it works as long as the NVA does SNAT. Use this as general Azure troubleshooting evidence; it does not establish Atlas-specific behavior or universal cross-spoke connectivity. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/networking/guide/private-link-hub-spoke-network ; https://msandbu.org/private-endpoints-snat-udr-and-azure-firewall/

evidence.quote:
The /32 route gets propagated to the following areas:

Any virtual network peering that you configure
The private endpoint sees the traffic based on the traffic flow and tries to route the packet back directly to the virtual machine.
Hi, as long as the NVA does SNAT then it would work.

edits.old: Ordinary Azure VNet peering is nontransitive. Peering an application spoke to a hub and the hub to an Atlas VNet does not alone provide an application-to-Atlas path; additional routing or direct connectivity is required. This limitation differs from accessing an endpoint located inside the directly peered hub. (high confidence)
edits.new: Ordinary Azure VNet peering is nontransitive: peering an application spoke to a hub and the hub to another VNet does not by itself connect the spoke to that other VNet; additional peering, routing or direct connectivity is required. This is general Azure behavior; the sources do not address Atlas VNets specifically. By contrast, MongoDB Atlas documents that a private endpoint inside a VNet can be reached from another VNet peered to the endpoint-connected VNet. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/networking/architecture/hub-spoke ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-private-endpoint.md

MongoDB's Atlas docs state that private endpoint connections within a VNet can be made transitively from a peered VNet and from an on-premises data center over ExpressRoute.
